data.title: Peter Schiff Predicts Gold Boom, Says Political Shift Threatens To Send Inflation Soaring — ‘Sign Of Things To Come’
data.description:
Key points:
  • With major U.S. stock market indexes ending the week lower, gold mining stocks stood out as one of the market's strongest performers.
  • Schiff highlighted the surge in the VanEck Gold Miners ETF over the past week, arguing that the gains could be a precursor to a broader rally in gold.
  • Higher inflation has historically strengthened gold's appeal among investors seeking protection against declining purchasing power.

Gold mining stocks emerged as a rare bright spot during a difficult week for equities, drawing attention from longtime gold bull Peter Schiff. The economist sees the rally as a potential signal of a much bigger move ahead for precious metals.

In a post on X, Schiff argued that a political shift to the left could fuel higher inflation, creating an especially favorable environment for gold. He pointed to the latest gains in gold mining stocks as an early indication of what's coming.

Gold Miners Surge, Schiff Sees Inflation-Driven Rally Ahead

With major U.S. stock market indexes ending the week lower, gold mining stocks stood out as one of the market's strongest performers.

Schiff highlighted the surge in the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) over the past week, arguing that the gains could be a precursor to a broader rally in gold.

“This is a sign of things to come. A sharp turn to the left, and the higher inflation that will result, will be extremely bullish for gold,” he said.

He argued about the prospect of a shift in political priorities leading to policies that put additional upward pressure on prices. Higher inflation has historically strengthened gold's appeal among investors seeking protection against declining purchasing power.

However, the latest move in gold miners comes against a backdrop of considerable volatility in the underlying metal.

Shares of gold miners Newmont Corp. (NEM), Agnico Eagle Mines Ltd. (AEM), Barrick Mining Corp. (B), and Franco-Nevada Corp. (FNV) soared between 10% and 16% this week.

Gold Rebounds From One-Year Low, But ING Sees Challenges Ahead

Spot gold prices recovered this week after three weeks of decline, with the yellow metal registering its best week since August.

According to analysts at ING Think, the rebound was supported by bargain hunting and a pullback in oil prices as signs of easing U.S.-Iran tensions helped ease some inflation concerns that had weighed on the metal.

However, the firm cautioned that gold's recovery could face obstacles in the near term. The precious metal has been caught in a broader risk-off move alongside heavy selling in technology stocks, while expectations of higher interest rates and a stronger U.S. dollar have weighed on investor sentiment.

The firm expects gold to regain some ground following its recent correction but sees limited scope for a sustained recovery while those headwinds persist.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, gained 0.17%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) rose 0.21%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged up by 0.06%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

data.title: Crusoe Completes Wyoming AI Data Center Development, Sells Site To Google
data.description:
OTTAWA (dpa-AFX) - Crusoe, an AI infrastructure and data center developer, said Google has acquired its data center site in southeast Wyoming, completing Crusoe's role in the project's early-stage development and advancing Google's expansion of AI and cloud infrastructure in the region.

The transaction marks the culmination of Crusoe's pre-development work for the Wyoming campus, which included site selection, securing governmental approvals, and developing a power strategy for the project. Financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed.

Crusoe and Tallgrass Energy jointly initiated the Wyoming campus by developing both power and data center infrastructure in parallel. The effort involved coordinating energy system design, data center engineering, site development, and engagement with hyperscale customers to prepare the site for large-scale deployment.

The sale highlights Crusoe's strategy of developing AI-ready infrastructure projects and transitioning them to major technology companies. The company recently disclosed that it is serving as the developer for Google's data center campus currently under construction in Armstrong County near Amarillo, Texas.

The Wyoming acquisition further strengthens Google's data center footprint as demand for computing capacity accelerates amid growing artificial intelligence workloads, while allowing Crusoe to focus on advancing additional AI infrastructure developments.

data.title: Muhurat Trading Strategy Diwali Day 2026: What to do, what to buy, what to avoid? Trading guide for Nov 8 - Key levels
data.description:
Muhurat Trading 2026, Nov. 7 -- The Indian stock market will open for its annual Muhurat trading session on Sunday, November 8, marking the beginning of Samvat 2083. The special Diwali session is considered an auspicious occasion to start investing and review financial goals. However, investors should not let the festive sentiment drive impulsive decisions.

With limited liquidity during the session and benchmark indices nearing important resistance levels, analysts recommend a cautious, stock-specific approach. While long-term investors can use the occasion to review their portfolios and make selective investments, short-term traders should watch key technical levels, track global cues and avoid aggressive positions.

Analysts believe Muhurat trading offers investors an opportunity to review their asset allocation, assess whether their portfolios are aligned with their financial goals and rebalance where necessary. They favour a stock-specific approach to long-term investing, while advising caution during the short trading window.

Liquidity is typically limited during the special session, making it inadvisable to place large orders or undertake aggressive buying and selling. New investors can consider token investments in fundamentally strong companies they are interested in holding for the long term. Investors should avoid buying stocks merely because it is an auspicious occasion and instead focus on valuations, business fundamentals and their investment objectives.

Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOSL) said Nifty valuations were attractive at 17.5 times forward earnings, 16% below the long-term average. However, it noted that small-cap stocks continued to trade at a 25% premium to their long-term average, warranting selectivity.

"We perceive FY27 to mark a return to double-digit earnings growth, with Nifty EPS expected to grow 16%/14% YoY in FY27/FY28 vs 5% in FY26. Nifty valuations are attractive at 17.5x forward earnings, 16% below the long-term average," MOSL said.

For Samvat 2083, MOSL favours banking and financial services, capital markets, manufacturing, global outsourcing and exports, consumption and digital businesses. It sees opportunities in healthcare devices, aerospace, auto components, pharmaceutical ingredients, garments, port cargo, organised jewellery and quick-commerce platforms.

The market's technical setup will be important during Sunday's Muhurat trading session, with both benchmark indices approaching resistance zones after a recent rally. Hitesh Tailor, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking, expects a sideways-to-consolidative session and has identified immediate support and resistance levels for Nifty and Bank Nifty. Traders will also need to track geopolitical developments, crude oil prices and global market cues before taking positions.

"For Muhurat trading, the overall market bias is likely to remain sideways to consolidative after the recent sharp upside move, as both benchmark indices are approaching crucial resistance zones. Nifty is trading around 24,600," Tailor said.

Tailor identified immediate support for Nifty at 24,350 and resistance in the 24,700-24,800 range, where rejection was visible. He cautioned that profit booking could emerge after six consecutive sessions of gains, particularly amid geopolitical concerns, crude oil volatility and the global market sell-off seen in US markets on November 5 and early Asian trading on November 6.

For Bank Nifty, the 57,500-57,800 range is important, with stronger resistance at 58,000-58,400 and support around 56,000-56,300. The support zone coincides with the index's 200-day exponential moving average and a previous trendline breakout area.

Tailor advised traders to monitor global cues and geopolitical developments and wait for a clear directional move instead of taking aggressive positions. Long-term investors, meanwhile, can use technical retracements to accumulate fundamentally strong stocks at lower levels with a longer-term perspective.

Meanwhile, Sumeet Bagadia placed Nifty 50's immediate support at 24,800-24,850 and resistance at 25,130-25,200 at the beginning of Samvat 2083.

data.title: WULF Stock Rebounds From Lowest Close In Over A Year, B. Riley Says Selloff ‘In No Way’ Justified
data.description:
Key points:
  • B. Riley analyst Nick Giles reiterated a 'Buy' rating on TeraWulf.
  • He called it one of the highest-quality names in its high-performance computing coverage.
  • The company’s third-quarter revenue jumped over 51% year-over-year to $76.2 million.

TeraWulf (WULF) shares rebounded from their lowest point in over a year on Friday, after the company reported its third-quarter results, with B.Riley saying the recent selloff was “in no way” justified for the stock.

The stock ended Friday’s session at around $11, while on Thursday, it closed at $10 before briefly dipping to $9, its lowest price in more than a year. Despite Friday’s gain, shares were still down over 3% for the week.

WULF stock closed up over 12% on Friday. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around WULF improved to the ‘bullish’ zone from ‘neutral,’ accompanied by ‘high’ chatter levels over the past day.

Why B.Riley Is Betting Big On WULF Stock

According to TheFly, B. Riley analyst Nick Giles reiterated a ‘Buy’ rating on the stock, adding that the company's HPC lease income nearly doubled from the prior quarter. Giles added that the recent selloff in shares was "in no way" justified for the stock.

Giles said the “next major catalyst” will be when the financing for TeraWulf’s Anthropic (ANT) lease is secured. He called the company “one of the highest-quality names in our HPC coverage.” The deal would help ease the concerns about funding and dilution that have been hanging over the stock, Giles said.

The 20-year lease covered roughly 401 megawatts of computing power at TeraWulf's Justified campus and is expected to generate about $19 billion during its first term.

The company announced on Tuesday that Alphabet Inc.’s (GOOG, GOOGL) Google was set to provide a credit backdrop to the firm. TeraWulf expects the first parts of the campus to be ready by the end of 2027 and the rest to follow in the second quarter of 2028.

Data Center Leases Drive Revenue

TeraWulf reported third-quarter revenue of $76.2 million, about 51% higher than $50.6 million a year ago. The company's revenue was 19% above analyst expectations of $64.07 million, according to Koyfin.

Most of that revenue came from leasing data-center space for high-performance computing, with its HPC lease income rising to $63 million, up from $7.2 million a year earlier. Bitcoin (BTC) mining revenue dropped to $13.2 million from $43.4 million.

Net income stood at $709.9 million, with most of it driven by a non-cash gain of $728.4 million. That gain stems from changes in the valuation of the company's warrant and derivative liabilities, the company said.

The company reported an adjusted loss of $0.03 per share, compared with the $0.38 loss that analysts expected, according to Koyfin data.

data.title: NSE's Electronic Gold Receipts record over ₹23 crore turnover on debut: How investors can buy
data.description:
Electronic Gold Receipts (EGRs) worth approximately ₹23.34 crore changed hands on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on November 6, as trading in the segment backed by gold infrastructure company Augmont Enterprises witnessed activity on its opening day.

According to data shared by Augmont, 1,60,357 EGR units were traded by around 4:25 pm on Friday (November 6). The company said the segment saw active buying and selling, with prices moving in a range of ₹1,450.50 to ₹1,460 during the session. The bid-ask spread remained between ₹0.50 and ₹1.

The trading activity follows the collaboration between NSE and Augmont to develop the EGR ecosystem, which allows investors to hold and trade receipts representing ownership of physical gold through a demat account.

What are Electronic Gold Receipts?

EGRs are exchange-traded securities backed by physical gold stored in regulated vaults. They allow investors to buy and sell gold through the stock exchange without having to physically store the metal themselves.

The receipts are held in dematerialised form, like shares, and can be traded through a stockbroker. NSE offers EGR contracts in different denominations, including 100 milligrams, 1 gram, 10 grams, 100 grams and 1 kg, subject to the applicable product specifications.

The gold backing the receipts is stored with registered vault managers. Investors can continue holding the EGRs in their demat accounts or opt for physical delivery by following the prescribed withdrawal process. Physical withdrawal may involve additional charges, including storage, testing and transportation costs.

EGR trades follow a T+1 settlement cycle, meaning the securities and funds are transferred on the next working day after the trade.

How can investors buy EGRs?

Investors need an active trading and demat account with a stockbroker that offers access to the NSE's EGR segment. They can then place buy and sell orders through the broker's trading platform, similar to transactions in listed shares.

However, EGR trading is not necessarily available through every stockbroking platform. Investors should check with their existing broker whether it has enabled the EGR segment before attempting to place an order.

For instance, Zerodha's support page currently says that it does not support EGR trading, although the facility is expected to be enabled. This highlights the limited availability of the product across brokerage platforms.

What should investors check before buying?

Apart from the prevailing market price, investors should check the denomination and purity of the EGR contract, brokerage and depository charges, and any applicable vault storage charges.

Those considering physical delivery should also check the withdrawal process, minimum delivery quantity and associated charges with the relevant vault manager.

While EGRs provide an exchange-based route to hold gold, investors should also consider liquidity and the availability of buyers and sellers before placing orders.

data.title: Delhi HC says entire book cannot be stopped over few disputed passages; modifies restraint on 'Yes Man'
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Drawing a distinction between restraining specific allegedly defamatory material and stopping an entire published work, the Delhi High Court has held that a pre-trial injunction against a book cannot extend beyond the passages found, at the interim stage, to warrant such protection.

In a significant ruling for authors and publishers, the High Court modified a blanket restraint imposed on "Yes Man: The Untold Story of Rana Kapoor", authored by Pavan Chand Lall and published by HarperCollins, allowing the remaining portions of the book to remain outside the scope of the injunction.

Justice Harish Vaidyanathan Shankar held that the restraint would operate only against four specific passages identified in the trial court's order and not against the book in its entirety.

The Court found no reason, at the interim stage, to interfere with the trial court's findings concerning three statements held to be prima facie defamatory and one statement characterised as derogatory. However, it ruled that these findings could not form the basis for restraining the publication, sale, distribution and circulation of the entire literary work.

The ruling assumes significance for the scope of interim restrictions on books and other published material, particularly before a court has conducted a full trial on allegations of defamation.

The High Court stressed that an interlocutory injunction affecting publication should be confined to what is necessary to address the specific injury found at the interim stage.

The Court noted that the trial court had examined several statements challenged by former Yes Bank co-founder Rana Kapoor but had not found all of them to be defamatory. Only three statements were held to be prima facie defamatory, while one was characterised as derogatory.

Despite this, the operative direction had restrained the book as a whole. The High Court held that such a broad consequence could not be sustained.

"The remaining contents of the Subject Book have not been found, at this stage, to constitute defamatory or derogatory material," the Court noted while concluding that the restraint should remain confined to the four passages in question.

It said the narrower restraint would protect Kapoor against further dissemination of the specific imputations found prima facie objectionable without imposing an unnecessary restriction on the rest of the book.

Justice Shankar also underlined that findings recorded while considering interim relief are provisional and cannot be treated as a final adjudication of the dispute.

The Court clarified that the issues of truth, justification, fair comment, privilege and other defences would have to be examined at trial after a fuller adjudication.

The judgment, therefore, does not finally determine whether the allegations made in the disputed passages are true or false, nor does it amount to a final verdict on author Pavan Chand Lall's research, sources or defence to the defamation claim.

The Court further emphasised that an interlocutory injunction is intended to prevent apprehended injury during the pendency of proceedings and not to grant relief wider than the injury which has been found sufficient to warrant protection.

The dispute relates to "Yes Man: The Untold Story of Rana Kapoor", which examines the life and career of Kapoor in the context of the rise and subsequent crisis of Yes Bank.

The book was published on December 22, 2020 and had remained in circulation for a considerable period before the trial court passed its injunction on July 10, 2024.

The High Court recorded that the affairs of Yes Bank and Kapoor's role had attracted extensive public scrutiny, particularly after proceedings were initiated by the Enforcement Directorate and the Central Bureau of Investigation in March 2020. The developments had also received substantial coverage in print and electronic media.

The wider subject matter of the book was among the circumstances relevant to the Court's consideration of restrictions on its publication.

The judgment also reflects judicial caution regarding restraints imposed before a full trial, particularly where such orders affect literary works already in the public domain.

The High Court said an injunction operating upon publication ought to be no wider than necessary, and courts must remain conscious that interim findings are provisional.

It ultimately held that protecting a person's reputation against specific imputations found prima facie objectionable could be achieved without withdrawing an entire book from circulation.

The High Court accordingly modified the July 2024 order to provide that the injunction would apply only to the portions containing Statements (ii), (iv), (vii) and (x), as identified by the trial court.

The remaining portions of the book would not be covered by the injunction merely because of the findings concerning those four statements.

The Court clarified that its observations were confined to the scope of interim relief and should not be construed as a final expression of opinion on the merits of the allegations or the defences available to the parties.

The trial court will now proceed to adjudicate the defamation suit on its merits, uninfluenced by the High Court's observations except to the extent expressly determined for deciding the interim relief.
